A0230.title: Action Safety Boundary & Permission Convergence
A0230.definition: Setting physical action safety boundaries (workspace, speed, force limits) for embodied agents, with human confirmation for hazardous actions and least-privilege execution, to prevent jailbreak or over-autonomy from causing irreversible physical consequences.
A0230.description:
Action safety boundary & permission convergence builds a hard-constraint layer against the risk of embodied agents performing dangerous physical actions when jailbroken or over-autonomous. First, physical action safety boundaries limit the robotic arm workspace, movement speed, and gripper force; commands exceeding boundaries are intercepted at the hardware layer and cannot be overridden by the VLA/LLM. Second, hazardous-action human confirmation requires real-time operator confirmation for high-risk actions such as opening doors, handling sharp objects, or transporting heavy loads. Third, least-privilege execution grants the agent only the minimum action permissions needed for the current task, auto-revoked at task end.

This measure is a key safety mechanism distinguishing embodied intelligence from pure software agents — software-agent misoperations can be rolled back, but embodied-agent physical actions are irreversible and require hardware-level hard constraints as a backstop. It works with A0225 (physical-world prompt injection detection) and A0072 (algorithm audit mechanism).
A0230.limitation: Over-strict boundaries limit task capability, affecting agent autonomy and efficiency; human confirmation in emergencies adds latency and may miss the best intervention window; boundary configuration needs per-task tuning, and general boundaries cannot fit all scenarios; the hardware constraint layer itself may be bypassed by firmware vulnerabilities, requiring pairing with secure boot.
